correctness.rationale: For each unit-edge M_{2n}, n≥3, the shortest-path profile f(k)=min(k,n+1−k) on 0≤k≤n is exact by cycle/opposite-jump parity. Thus D is a real symmetric 2n-circulant. Fourier transforming its discrete second difference at profile corners gives nonpositive even-index eigenvalues and, at odd j, (−1)^((j+1)/2)csc(πj/(2n)) for odd n or the corresponding cotangent for even n. Among positive reflected frequencies, j=3 gives the unique largest eigenvalue (one real dimension at n=3; 2 otherwise). Its strict positivity rules out squared-Hilbert embedding by conditional negative definiteness; Taylor series establish parity tails. Independent BFS-built matrix eigenanalysis corroborated all n=3,…,23; the corner algebra proves all n.
